newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-STUTTGART SELL ELBER TO BAYERN, BUY AKPOBORIE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-STUTTGART SELL ELBER TO BAYERN, BUY AKPOBORIE.

text.p: VfB Stuttgart said on Monday their Brazilian striker Giovane Elber would join Bayern Munich in the close season and Nigerian Jonathan Akpoborie would replace him.
Stuttgart president Gerhard Mayer-Vorfelder said the clubs were still negotiating the exact transfer fee for Elber but it would be more than 10 million marks ($5.8 million).
"This wasn't an easy decision for us," Mayer-Vorfelder said. "I'd like to have kept Giovane but only on the condition that he extend his contract. He didn't want to do that."

Elber is expected to slot into Juergen Klinsmann's position at Bayern. The Germany captain has decided to leave the club at the end of the season, although he has yet to decide where he will go. Italy's Parma are among the possibilities.
The exact fee for Akpoborie depends on the fate of his current club Hansa Rostock.

According to his contract, Stuttgart will pay five million marks ($2.9 million) if the east German club stay in the Bundesliga and four million ($2.3 million) if they are relegated. Rostock are currently one point above the relegation zone.

Elber and Akpoborie are two of the most exciting strikers in the Bundesliga. The Brazilian, who is keen to improve his chances of playing for his country by moving to Germany's highest-profile club, has scored 16 league goals this season.

Akpoborie has scored 13 of Rostock's 30 Bundesliga goals this season. Stuttgart coach Joachim Loew, who has extended his own contract at the club until 1999, said the Nigerian was an ideal replacement for Elber.
"He's got a good character and he knows the Bundesliga," Loew said.
